knowledge:
- key_parameters: names=A character vector of platform or condition names ;; data=A list of matrices containing genomic measurements for each platform, which must have identical dimensions, row names, and column names ;; type=The parameter to plot in plotMarginals or plotMostDiscordant, which can be "average", "sensitivity", or "precision" ;; n=The number of most discordant features to display in the heatmap generated by plotMostDiscordant
- alternatives: Defining a single "gold standard" (such as qPCR) to validate new technologies, which can introduce bias towards that standard. The consensus package offers an empirical, multi-platform alternative.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have matched samples measured across three or more different genomic platforms, laboratory protocols, or experimental conditions, and you want to assess and compare their measurement quality (sensitivity, precision, and dynamic range) without assuming any single platform is the absolute truth.
- pitfalls: The input matrices for all platforms must have identical dimensions, row names (features/loci), and column names (samples). If these do not match exactly, MultiMeasure will throw an error indicating which attributes are mismatched.

workflows.name: cross_platform_consensus_analysis
workflows.intent: Fit row-linear models to cross-platform genomic measurements to compare platform sensitivity, precision, and dynamic range, and identify highly discordant features.
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and data ;; 2. Construct a MultiMeasure object using MultiMeasure() ;; 3. Visualize a single gene fit using plotOneFit() ;; 4. Fit the consensus model using fitConsensus() ;; 5. Plot marginal distributions of average, sensitivity, and precision using plotMarginals() ;; 6. Identify and plot the most discordant genes using plotMostDiscordant()
workflows.code:
library(consensus)
data("TCGA")
tcga_mm <- MultiMeasure(names=c("U133A", "Huex", "Agilent", "RNA-Seq"), 
                        data=list(U133A, Huex, Agilent, RNASeq))
plotOneFit(tcga_mm, "TP53", brewer.pal(n = 4, name = "Dark2"))
fit <- fitConsensus(tcga_mm)
plotMarginals(fit, "average", brewer.pal(n = 4, name = "Dark2"))
plotMarginals(fit, "sensitivity", brewer.pal(n = 4, name = "Dark2"))
plotMarginals(fit, "precision", brewer.pal(n = 4, name = "Dark2"))
plotMostDiscordant(fit, "sensitivity", 15)
plotOneFit(tcga_mm, "MYO7B", brewer.pal(n = 4, name = "Dark2"))
